title: Lambert, Hendricks & Ross and muscle memory
summary: How Jon Hendricks sings so fast: tedious repetition; Gates on watching himself on video and Freddie Freeloader.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Okay I got one more for you here. This has always mystified me. © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
Oh that’s Jon. Is that the live recording in San Francisco or something like that?
That came from the LP. I just don’t know, how does a person articulate that fast?

It’s muscle memory. You just do it so many times, so many times, so many times, that it’s muscle memory. I mean I watch somebody like you play the piano I say wow, man. I mean I can play anything as long as it’s rubato. But when I see people play I say how do people do that? Well, they practice. And here’s one that I came up with. Some people call it rehearsal. Some people call it practicing. I call it what it really is: tedious repetition. You do it enough times you’re going to get good at it. You keep doing it, keep doing it, keep doing it, until you don’t have to think about it. Then it just happens. Then you can enjoy it while it’s happening as opposed to working at it to get it through. You say, yeah, I’m along for the ride. And I think that’s what people like Jon did. Because when I started to learn that kind of material I said, “how do they get this off?” Well you do it until you’ve got it. And you have to listen to yourself, and you have to be critical enough to say — I mean the first time I saw myself videotaped, videotaped, you know, VHS? I went to — I was given the videotape but I went to a lady friend’s house, because she had a VHS player and I didn’t. So we watched and it was like 25 minutes. And then it was over and she got up to go into the kitchen to make a cup of tea or something, and I rewound it and started to watch it again. And she came back into the living room and she said, “oh you like to watch yourself, don’t you.” I said, “on the contrary, this is making me really uncomfortable. But I’m going to watch this to find out what I don’t like and try to fix it.” So I think that’s what you have to do. If you’re satisfied with it all the time then it’s not going to go anywhere. But I think that that rapid fire — you have to be inclined to want to do that, and have maybe the possibility of getting it off. But you have to work at it. You don’t just do it. I mean Jon Hendricks is amazing. He’s amazing. And every time I would get something of his I’d say, “wow, this is the better than the last one.” And then I mean “Freddie Freeloader,” did you ever hear that?
It’s amazing what he wrote, and that he sings a John Coltrane solo. I mean who could sing a John Coltrane solo? Jon Hendricks.
